rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact block in all four views, so it avoids the obvious one-view-only failure and the geometry is not colliding. The dominant mass is legible, but it is still mostly a generic stepped/grid extrusion with limited spatial generosity at the street edge. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged only weakly: the ground response does not clearly open into a public court or seam on the access side, so the access relation remains semantically underdeveloped. The top view suggests some internal striping/voiding, but that void is not yet expressed as a convincing public figure or threshold in the elevation views. Programmatically, neighborhood living can support a compact mass with active ground and one clear public void or terrace; this candidate is plausible but not yet convincing enough to hard-pass because the active threshold and public-space logic are too faint and the section reads more like stacked solids than a mixed-use street building with a legible ground condition.
